name: Wat Tyler
role: Elected leader of the Kentish rebels
description: Almost entirely undocumented before 7 June 1381, when the Anonimalle Chronicle records his election as leader of the Kentish rebels at a mass gathering in Maidstone. Chroniclers' accounts of his origin vary and are not independently corroborated -- he is variously said to have been from Essex or Kent, and to have served as an archer in France; none of this can be verified against an independent record, and this book treats it as unconfirmed tradition rather than fact. He led the Kentish contingent to Blackheath and into London on 13 June, presided over the destruction of the Savoy Palace and the Tower killings, negotiated the Mile End charter's Kentish equivalent, and on 15 June met Richard II at Smithfield to present a further set of demands (per the Anonimalle Chronicle: a charter, the abolition of the episcopal hierarchy, redistribution of church wealth, and a single law of the land). An altercation there -- accounts differ on exactly what triggered it -- ended with Lord Mayor William Walworth striking him and squire Ralph Standish finishing the killing. Tyler was beheaded; his head was displayed on London Bridge.
narrative_function: The rebellion's field commander and chief negotiator; his death at Smithfield ends the London phase of the revolt within minutes.
